setup: Pulleys at shoulder height or a little above
Cross the cables: each hand takes the far one
Stand centred, arms straight out in front
Keep a soft bend in your elbows
execution: Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc
Stop when your arms line up with your body
Keep the elbow bend the same throughout
Return slowly until your hands nearly meet
faults: Don't bend your elbows into a row
Don't arch your back to finish

notes: Use light weights. The rear delts are small, and the movement should stay slow and controlled.
Each arm pulls its own stack. Log the reading on one stack and set both the same.
Check both handles are clipped on firmly and the space around you is clear.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at shoulder height, figure centred between two cable columns, pulleys at about shoulder height. Cable lines from each pulley cross in front of the figure to the opposite hand.

keyPositions.label: Crossed
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall between the columns. Arms reaching straight forward at shoulder height, hands close together in front of the chest, cables crossed. Elbows softly bent.

keyPositions.label: Open
keyPositions.describe: Arms swept out to the sides at shoulder height, in line with the body, like a T. Elbow bend unchanged; shoulders down; no backward lean.

ikHints: Each cable runs straight from its pulley to the opposite hand
emphasise: Slow return with the cables crossing
